# axe-core (vendored, unmodified)

- Project: axe-core, accessibility rules engine by Deque Systems, Inc.
- Upstream source: <https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core>, tag `v4.14.0`
  (the unminified source is the repository's `axe.js` at that tag and in the npm package `axe-core@4.14.0`).
- File shipped: `4.14.0/axe.min.js`, byte-identical to the file in the npm package `axe-core@4.14.0`.
- SHA-256: `20c09fe157a8a34a30e241aaa1fcdade657734f08ab379ecfbeb7d45cc46e878`
  (matches `sri-history.json` of that package: `sha256-IMCf4Veoo0ow4kGqofza3mV3NPCKs3ns++t9RcxG6Hg=`).
- Copyright (c) 2015 - 2026 Deque Systems, Inc.
- Licence: Mozilla Public License 2.0, text in `4.14.0/LICENSE-MPL-2.0`. The file keeps its
  original MPL header, which must stay in every copy. Its bundled third-party components keep
  their own licences in `4.14.0/LICENSE-3RD-PARTY.txt`.

## What this means for rightkit-browser

- The MPL is file-level copyleft. `axe.min.js` is unmodified, so it stays under the MPL and the
  rest of the crate stays `MIT OR Apache-2.0`. Do not edit this file; to change it, replace it
  with another upstream release and update the version, hash and this notice together
  (`AXE_VERSION` and `AXE_SHA256` in `src/capture.rs`).
- The crate verifies the embedded bytes against `AXE_SHA256` before every use and refuses to run
  an axe check on a mismatch.
- The file is compiled in only with the Cargo feature `axe` (off by default), so a consumer that
  does not enable it ships no MPL-covered file. cargo-deny's `licenses.allow` lists `MPL-2.0` for
  unmodified dependencies; this is the same unmodified-use basis, applied to a vendored file.
- Source availability (MPL section 3.2): the complete source of the covered file is the upstream
  tag named above, which this notice points to.
